prompt: A two-tree range-sum implementation multiplies the difference-tree prefix by the queried position. Why must it subtract a second tree’s weighted prefix?

options.text: To remove all elements inside the updated range.
options.explanation: Those elements are exactly the contributions the result must retain.

options.text: To undo every previous range update.
options.explanation: Queries must preserve all updates that contribute to the prefix.

options.text: Because the first tree stores maximum values rather than differences.
To remove contributions from positions before each difference began.
options.explanation: Correct. Repeating each difference across the whole prefix initially overcounts its earlier positions.

workedExample: A difference beginning partway through the array contributes only from its own position onwards. Multiplying its value by the length of the entire prefix counts too many positions. The weighted tree records the positions before that start, so subtracting it leaves exactly the wanted repetitions. End-boundary cancellation also stops a range’s contribution growing after its right end.
